item.title: Bruno Fernandes’ house burgled while playing for Man Utd in Champions League
item.description: Manchester United are offering full support to Bruno Fernandes and his family after a burglary at his home while he was playing in a Champions league clash against Como on Wednesday evening. A damaging evening in Lombardy saw United fall to a heavy 4-1 defeat against Cesc Fabregas’ side, lengthening their winless streak to seven matches and prompting Fernandes to openly criticise the tactics of boss Michael Carrick . Having flown back from Italy alongside his teammates early on Thursday morning, the Portuguese international was forced to handle the fallout from the break-in that occurred during his time abroad. It is understood that Fernandes’ family were not present when the incident occurred, with officers attending promptly and United giving full assistance to their skipper. Fernandes, meanwhile, is set to escape internal punishment after the Manchester United captain’s outburst in Como. The defeat and Fernandes' statements intensified scrutiny over Carrick’s position prior to Sunday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth, but it is understood he will remain in his post . United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season’s performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick’s tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week’s remarks by Lisandro Martinez. Bruno Fernandes questioned Michael Carrick’s tactics after the Como defeat (PA) Fernandes claimed it was the staff’s decision “not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind” in Como. Captain Fernandes, who was substituted after 67 minutes at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, delivered a damning assessment after the game. He told TNT Sports: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind, and trying to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball. “Sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams, they get confidence. They have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work.” Asked further about the tactics, he said: “It’s on the manager and on the staff to say it, it is not on me. “I just said that I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable, as they did to us.” Yet, the Press Association understands United are not expected to punish Fernandes for his impassioned post-match interview a week on from Martinez’s caustic remarks, which led to a fine and talks with the club hierarchy.

"There's a lot of nerves, especially because it's gonna be a really big game," freshman defender Maddie Halliburton said. "But I'm actually just really excited that we got all this far." Boerne Champion (25-3) faces League City Clear Creek (32-3-1) at 1:30 p.m. Friday afternoon in the state semifinals. The winner plays Austin Westlake or Hebron in the boys state finals at noon Saturday. Boerne Champion's boys team has qualified for the state tournament for five straight seasons. item.title: Sarri: ‘Atalanta more positive than negative, unexpected defeat to Ajax’
item.description: Sarri: ‘Atalanta more positive than negative, unexpected defeat to Ajax’ Maurizio Sarri sees ‘more positives than negatives’ from Atalanta’s 2-0 Conference League loss to Ajax . ‘Going into the last five minutes, the last thing I was thinking about was defeat.’ La Dea had some good scoring opportunities and a decent amount of possession in Amsterdam, but were ultimately undone by two late errors. The first saw youth academy product Relja Obric muscled off a long ball by Tolu Arodokare, then Abdella Ouazane blasted in off the underside of the bar from the tightest of angles for the 2-0 result. Sarri irritated with Atalanta defeat AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS – OCTOBER 22: Michel, Head Coach of Ajax, a Maurizio Sarri, Head Coach of Atalanta BC, before the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AFC Ajax and Atalanta BC at Johan Cruijff Arena on October 22, 2026 in Amsterdam, Netherlands. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) “We made a mistake and it cost us a goal, but it’s not as if we can blame the lads too much for that,” Sarri told Sky Sport Italia. “The second half we were under pressure, but managed to create numerous chances on the counter, but we failed to make the most of those situations. It was a performance of tempo and intensity, worthy of the European level against a good team. “Going into the last five minutes, the last thing I was thinking about was a defeat, because the situation seemed to be favourable for us. I am sorry for our fans, so many came here to see us.” It was the second senior game for Obric, who also made a costly error in his senior debut at the weekend in a 3-2 Serie A defeat to Milan. This has been a baptism of fire for the youngster, who was forced to play due to a growing injury crisis in defence. AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS – OCTOBER 22: Players of Atalanta BC pose for a team photograph before the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AFC Ajax and Atalanta BC at Johan Cruijff Arena on October 22, 2026 in Amsterdam, Netherlands. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) “We need a result to get out of this, but we mustn’t leave the stadium tonight feeling distraught,” insisted Sarri. “A little angry, maybe frustrated, but not distraught, because it was a strong performance, we showed improvement in some areas, and there are more positives than negatives to take from this game.” Atalanta were swarming around Ajax on several occasions, but didn’t manage to finish off the move or even truly test Marc-Andre ter Stegen. “I agree, at this level you cannot have three on two and not even get a shot on target. I also want to note we should not have left Obric alone against an opponent who is taller and stronger, there should’ve been help from his teammates.” AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS – OCTOBER 22: Eljif Elmas of Atalanta BC shoots under pressure from Youri Baas of Ajax during the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AFC Ajax and Atalanta BC at Johan Cruijff

item.title: Jason Wilcox vs. Christopher Vivell: Tensions rising between Man United chiefs over major decision
item.description: Jason Wilcox vs. Christopher Vivell: Tensions rising between Man United chiefs over major decision Manchester United executives Jason Wilcox and Christopher Vivell are reportedly at odds with each other over a major club decision. Turmoil United are once again in a turbulent state amidst their woeful start to the season. After a poor summer window in which several areas were overlooked, United are enduring a dreadful run of form that has seen them go seven games without a victory. The Red Devils have registered just two wins across all competitions this term: against Ipswich Town in the Premier League and Sabah FK in the Champions League. They were knocked out of the Carabao Cup at the first time of asking by Brighton & Hove Albion. United stooped to a new all-time low on Wednesday as they were beaten 4-1 by Como in the Champions League. Following this latest disappointing result, Michael Carrick finds himself in a highly precarious position, with his departure seemingly only a matter of time. After the final whistle, Carrick blamed his players for not working hard enough, while skipper Bruno Fernandes aimed a dig at the manager’s tactics. A recent report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that members of the United hierarchy were left shocked by the team’s woeful performance in Italy. Carrick will take charge of Sunday’s meeting against Bournemouth but links to his potential replacements are gathering pace, with the likes of Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler and Julian Nagelsmann being lined up. According to the Daily Mail , there are growing tensions between Wilcox and Vivell regarding the choice of manager to replace Carrick. Rift emerging The newspaper claims, “Manchester United’s problems are piling up with there understood to be growing tensions between director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell.” “Speaking to a handful of key figures close to the dressing room, each of whom are in regular dialogue with the United hierarchy, Daily Mail Sport has learned that along with disagreements on the pitch between players and manager, there is also growing discontent in the boardroom.” “Wilcox and Vivell are said to have differing opinions on who should succeed Michael Carrick, should the decision be made to move on to a third manager in 2026.” It is understood that Vivell is pushing hard for Nagelsmann, while Wilcox is championing the appointment of a Premier League-tested coach such as Howe or Hurzeler. Nathan Salt explains that there is a degree of sympathy for Carrick, owing to a feeling that the players have let him down with their performances and lack of application. Carrick will speak to the media on Friday in his pre-match press conference for the Bournemouth meeting.

item.title: Bournemouth stun 10-man AC Milan to claim famous win in Europa League
item.description: Bournemouth's Amine Adli (C) celebrates scoring his side's third goal with teammates during the UEFA Europa League soccer match between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium. (is associated with: «Bournemouth stun 10-man AC Milan to claim famous win in Europa League») Andrew Matthews/PA Wire/dpa Bournemouth scaled giddy new heights in their debut Europa League campaign as 10-man AC Milan were convincingly brushed aside 3-0 at the Vitality Stadium. The Italian giants, champions of Serie A only four years ago, were wretched, unable to match Marco Rose’s team who pressed them ruthlessly and attacked breathlessly in torrential conditions on the south coast. The first two goals were penalties scored in the first half, by Justin Kluivert then by Marcus Tavernier, before Amine Adli added a magnificent late free-kick, but the home side ought to have had even more to show for their dominance. Mike Maignan, the Milan goalkeeper and captain, let his team and his manager Ruben Amorim down badly and inexplicably, swiping at the face of James Hill at a corner, conceding a spot-kick and leaving his side to play for more than an hour with 10 players. Bournemouth have looked perfectly at home on their maiden European adventure but, even so, this fixture had an almost surreal sound to it, the seven-time champions of Europe taking a hammering on a pitch that was hosting League Two football as recently as 2010. “How did we end up here?” read a huge tifo unfurled in the North Stand before kick-off, but Bournemouth’s display suggested this might be just the beginning for them in Europe.

item.description: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Did Colin Cowherd just reveal the underlying truth about Texas HC Steve Sarkisian’s coaching of Arch Manning? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Colin Cowherd had some insight to provide into the Texas Longhorns’ situation between Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning midway through the 2026 season. Texas got off to a promising start, winning its first four games and rising to No. 1 of the AP Top 25. They have since lost two consecutive games against Oklahoma and Florida in collapsing fashion, free falling down to 19th in the latest rankings. Cowherd did an episode of The Herd on Thursday, giving his stance into the situation. He believes the Manning family name is placing pressure on Sarkisian to not mess up Arch’s trajectory as a prospective professional player in the NFL. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “There is pressure to not screw up Arch Manning … I honestly think [Sark] is trying to protect his NFL career,” Cowherd said. “Arch should be running. It should be Tebow-esque. Texas should be running the ball 60 to 65 percent of the time. A total college offense leaning into Arch’s size and athletic ability, but if you do that, that’s not the NFL. Are you screwing with his NFL career? And I think Sark almost subliminally is not running the offense that is best for Arch. He’s building a pro-style offense, and that’s not really playing to his strengths.” "There is pressure to not screw up Arch Manning… I honestly think [Sark] is trying to protect his NFL career." @colincowherd doesn't think Sark is setting Arch up for success at Texas pic.twitter.com/5qyKPIt5f0 — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) October 22, 2026 What lies ahead for Steve Sarkisian, Texas Texas still has a chance to get its campaign back on track to be in the CFP mix. However, another loss would their hopes for the tournament and put an end to the dynamic between Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Texas has a 4-2 overall record this season, going 1-2 in its SEC contests so far. They sit at 12th place in the conference standings, being above the Texas A&M Aggies and the South Carolina Gamecocks while trailing the Oklahoma Sooners and the Auburn Tigers. item.title: Steelers’ Paris bar fan event’s fate sealed amid protests
item.description: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images. Steelers’ Paris bar fan event’s fate sealed amid protests appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers will no longer hold their planned Steelers House gathering in Paris this weekend after recent protests prompted security concerns around the event’s location. Pittsburgh canceled the fan gathering at a bar in the Bastille neighborhood ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints . The decision affects the team-sponsored event but does not change plans for Sunday’s game at Stade de France. “Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood, and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers House fan event in Paris,” a message sent to fans read, according to The Associated Press. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Steelers described the decision as a precaution after the Bastille area experienced recent disruptions. Additional demonstrations could also take place in Paris and other areas of France over the weekend. The NFL’s broader activities in the city have continued without interruption. Nicki Ewell, the league’s vice president for global events, told the AP that Pittsburgh made the call to cancel Steelers House. The NFL helped distribute the announcement after previously working with the team to promote the gathering. Ewell said other NFL fan events have not been affected. An Irish pub called O’Sullivans in the Bastille area had also advertised a watch party for Sunday’s Steelers-Saints matchup. Roger Goodell addresses security ahead of Steelers’ Paris clash The Steelers reiterated that the league continues to coordinate with local officials as preparations for the game continue. “The NFL, as they do for every game, including international games, is working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters,” the Steelers said in a statement to the AP. “As stated by the NFL, there have been no disruptions or impacts at League sites.” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell addressed the unrest Wednesday and expressed confidence that the league has taken the necessary precautions for its Paris game. Goodell said he spoke with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, while officials have remained in communication with authorities in Paris and throughout France. “We’ve made all the preparations,” Goodell said. “Protests are not unusual in France, as you know, and that’s something that we will be aware of and make sure that the appropriate arrangements are made.” The cancellation therefore remains limited to Pittsburgh’s designated Bastille bar event rather than Sunday’s game. The Steelers enter Week 7 at 4-2, while the Saints sit at 2-4. Pittsburgh and New Orleans will meet Sunday at Stade de France, with kickoff scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. item.title: ESPN catches Steve Kerr spewing Lakers referee conspiracy on hot mic
item.description: Credit: NBA on ESPN As the Golden State Warriors endured a frustrating season-opening loss, head coach Steve Kerr resorted to accusing the referees of giving Luka Dončić and the Los Angeles Lakers a clear home court advantage. With the Warriors trailing the Lakers 81-59 midway through the third quarter Wednesday night, Kerr pulled rookie Yaxel Lendeborg aside to offer the first-round draft pick some words of wisdom during the first game of his young NBA career. The conversation was likely meant to be private, but ESPN mics picked up Kerr’s comments. Steve Kerr CALLED OUT the Lakers whistle on the hot mic: “They call all that sh*t here, they wouldn’t call it in any other arena.” https://t.co/FjGzYPdqg9 — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) October 22, 2026 “It’s the bullsh*t in the NBA. They call all that sh*t here, they wouldn’t call it in any other arena,” Kerr told Lendeborg who picked up four fouls in 29 minutes. This coming from the head coach of a team that was widely accused of benefiting from illegal screens to generate open shots for Steph Curry and Klay Thompson during the height of their dynasty. But maybe Kerr never thought the Warriors benefited from those calls in the Lakers’ building. Dončić is often accused of receiving his own whistle advantage by foul-baiting and whining to officials. And Kerr appears to think it worked to the Lakers’ advantage Wednesday night, despite each team visiting the line 27 times. Lendeborg did receive a technical foul for trash talking with Dončić in the first half that probably wasn’t warranted. And after the game, Kerr’s words appeared to resonate with Lendeborg. Because while it may not have been the head coach’s intent, Lendeborg went off during his postgame press conference, claiming he lost all respect for Dončić after witnessing his whining and complaining firsthand. Kerr similarly defended Lendeborg in his own press conference, claiming the rookie was called for at least three fouls that would not have been called in any other league. But the Lakers got the last laugh, blowing out the Warriors 127-105 behind 28 points from Dončić. It’s hard to imagine the referees could have done much to overturn a 22-point blowout loss for Golden State, regardless of where the game was played. item.title: F1 Today: Hamilton details Singapore GP disaster as Horner speaks out on Red Bull return
item.description: From Lewis Hamilton explaining the costly strategy mistake that compromised his Singapore Grand Prix to Christian Horner ruling out a return to Red Bull more than a year after his dismissal, here are the main Formula 1 stories of the day. Hamilton reveals what went wrong with costly Singapore strategy gamble Lewis Hamilton has explained the circumstances behind his unsuccessful strategy gamble at the Singapore Grand Prix, admitting that he realised his decision to stay out was probably a mistake almost immediately. Speaking to the media ahead of the United States Grand Prix, the seven-time world champion revealed that he wanted to pursue a different strategy from Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, believing that following the same approach would limit his chances of challenging Max Verstappen for victory. However, the gamble backfired. Hamilton struggled on the medium tyres during his opening stint before losing valuable time behind Leclerc. He later decided against entering the pit lane, unaware that his team-mate was coming in, and realised his mistake as he passed the pit entry. The Briton accepted responsibility for the decision but defended his willingness to challenge Ferrari's strategic approach. He also confirmed that discussions have taken place behind the scenes to improve collaboration, insisting that the setback will not discourage him from taking risks in pursuit of better results. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Horner makes Red Bull return stance clear after shock dismissal Christian Horner has ruled out the possibility of returning to Red Bull, bringing an end to speculation about a potential reunion with the team he led for two decades. The Briton was dismissed in July 2025, shortly after the British Grand Prix, ending a remarkable spell that saw Red Bull claim eight Drivers' Championships and six Constructors' Championships. Since his departure, the 52-year-old has been linked with a potential return to Formula 1. Speaking on Jodie Kidd's Kidd in a Sweet Shop YouTube channel, Horner reflected on his time at the Milton Keynes-based outfit, acknowledging that the final years of his tenure were difficult despite the team's considerable success. The former team principal confirmed that he remains on good terms with Red Bull's shareholders but made it clear that his chapter with the Austrian outfit is over. Horner has previously expressed an interest in returning to Formula 1, although only in a role that would allow him to compete for victories. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures

That means he's cautiously optimistic about the impact of the impending 24-team College Football Playoff, which will likely begin next season pending contractual agreements between the SEC, the Big Ten, other collegiate conferences and broadcast partner ESPN. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) "Opportunity is great," Sarkisian said Thursday during his weekly Zoom availability with reporters. "More teams get an opportunity to try to win a national championship." Sarkisian then reeled off a few reasons why more teams makes more sense, especially if a squad has to deal with some adversity in an early-season loss that once ended all title hopes. "Maybe you may have had to endure an injury or two," he said. "Maybe your quarterback was out. You get them back, and now you're healthy and you're fresh and you're better. Maybe it gives you an opportunity early in your season to play some younger players, knowing, hey, maybe we have a couple of losses that don't want to lose. item.title: Barcelona want to reinforce one position in January
item.description: Barcelona want to reinforce one position in January La Liga champions Barcelona are expected to seek out fresh blood in one key area of Hansi Flick’s squad with a view to the 2nd half of the campaign. This comes amid the understanding that Deco and co. will set about bringing in a new central defender in January. Barca are of course fresh off seeing their flawless opening to the new campaign brought to an end on Tuesday night. After making the trip to Paris to face European champions PSG, the Blaugrana were condemned to the wrong side of a 4-2 result. En route to defeat, the most glaring weakness in the visitors’ squad was laid bare, as the lack of depth at the heart of Hansi Flick’s backline was badly exposed. In turn, it should come as little surprise to hear of Deco and co. preparing to address this concern in the winter. As per a report from Fichajes : ‘Barcelona have an urgent need to resolve a problem they couldn’t address during the summer. Now, they face the task of signing a defender in the winter transfer window.’ Specifically, the Camp Nou brass are on the lookout for a new left-footed centre-back. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Bears Hit With Sudden Trade Suggestion to Pursue $105.8 Million Star
item.description: The Chicago Bears once again appear to be a serious contender in the NFC. After winning the NFC North division title last year and earning the No. 2 seed in the playoffs, the Bears are currently 4-2 after their Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons on the road. Caleb Williams made his return to the field against the Falcons. He completed 30 of his 36 pass attempts for 305 yards, a touchdown, and no interceptions. On paper, Chicago has the necessary talent to be a Super Bowl contender. However, there are still some clear holes the team could look to fill. With the NFL trade deadline coming up on November 10, rumors have started to fly. Ryan Poles has had a very aggressive approach in recent years. Fans should not expect to see that change before the deadline. If the right move presents itself, the Bears will almost certainly pounce. Keeping that in mind, one aggressive suggestion has been made that would see Chicago pursue a blockbuster trade for a $105.8 million star. Aug 26, 2023; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles looks on before a game against the Buffalo Bills at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Bartel-USA TODAY Sports Chicago Bears Named Potential Trade Destination for Jeffery Simmons The Athletic’s Daniel Popper recently created and publsihed a 2026 trade deadline big board. In that column, he suggested Chicago as a trade suitor for Tennessee Titans superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. “Simmons signed a three-year extension in June. The Titans, however, are going nowhere fast under first-year coach Robert Saleh. They earned their first win of the season over the Colts in Week 6. They are nonetheless trending toward another top-five pick, and dealing Simmons would present an opportunity to add valuable draft capital. Simmons is guaranteed $26.95 million in base salary in 2027. He is also due a $5.5 million option bonus in September,” Popper wrote . “Any acquiring team should be comfortable with those figures. Simmons is a game-wrecker as a run defender and pass rusher. item.title: McDermott calls for Super League to accept NRL investment
item.description: Brian McDermott enjoyed a trophy-laden spell as Leeds Rhinos coach between 2011-18 [Getty Images] England head coach Brian McDermott has called for Super League to accept investment from Australia's NRL in order to improve the English game. Talks are currently ongoing after Super League clubs rejected a £35m package from the Australian Rugby League Commission and a second deadline of 15 October was allowed to pass without an agreement being reached. Formalising a partnership between the sport's two leading competitions is seen as as a key step in helping to grow the European competition's revenue. "I think the NRL's investment in Super League could be very, very positive," said McDermott, who is also the assistant coach of the Gold Coast Titans. "The product's brilliant. It has always being brilliant. The product's never been the problem. The players have never been the problem. The coaches have never been the problem. "It's just how it's marketed and how it's presented to people. I think there's some dominoes could start falling our way if the NRL invests and we accept their investment." Super League is yet to agree a new title sponsorship deal, finalise broadcast negotiations or even its fixtures for the 2027 campaign with London Broncos' position yet to be fully determined. The Broncos came in16th on the yearly grading list, below fellow Championship side Barrow Raiders, despite a season in which they won the second tier's Grand Final, the 1895 Cup and were runaway champions in the regular-season standings. The Broncos were overlooked 12 months ago when Bradford Bulls, York Knights and Toulouse Olympique joined the expanded 14-team competition. But with the backing of Australian businessman Grant Wechsel and former Brisbane Broncos star Darren Lockyer, and with a squad full of internationals, they do still harbour hopes of playing in Super League in 2027. item.title: NASCAR Cup Series Preview: Championship Battle Heats Up at Talladega
item.description: Photo by: Jim Dedmon The NASCAR Cup Series heads to Talladega Superspeedway on Sunday for the YellaWood 500, a critical race as the championship Chase enters its final three events. With the title fight tightening, drivers cannot afford a poor finish, and Talladega’s unpredictable nature could dramatically reshape the standings. The 188 lap race is scheduled for 2 p.m. ET on NBC, with drivers preparing for another intense afternoon of superspeedway racing. Kyle Larson Looks to Protect His Championship Lead Kyle Larson enters the weekend leading the championship standings, but his advantage is far from comfortable. Christopher Bell sits just five points behind Larson, while Chase Briscoe, Denny Hamlin, Ryan Blaney and Joey Logano remain within striking distance. Larson needs a clean race after a disappointing result at Phoenix threatened to tighten the championship battle. Talladega presents a different challenge, as drivers must navigate massive drafting packs and avoid the accidents that frequently decide superspeedway races. Bell has an opportunity to take over the championship lead with a strong performance. Briscoe and Hamlin will also be looking to capitalize, knowing that a victory could provide a significant advantage heading into the final two races. Carson Hocevar Hopes to Recreate Talladega Magic Carson Hocevar will be one of the drivers to watch after winning the spring race at Talladega. The Spire Motorsports driver proved he can handle the pressure of a dramatic superspeedway finish, and another victory would further establish him as a serious threat at drafting tracks. Ryan Blaney is another contender. The Team Penske driver has a strong history at Talladega and knows how to position himself near the front when the race reaches its closing laps. Joey Logano, Austin Cindric and Tyler Reddick also have the potential to challenge for the victory. Team Penske’s drafting strength could be particularly important as drivers attempt to maintain momentum through the large packs. Talladega Could Change Everything The 2.66-mile superspeedway is known for close racing, aggressive blocking and last-lap drama. Drivers must balance the need to gain positions with the risk of getting caught in a multi-car accident. Stage points will be important for the championship contenders, but surviving the final laps could ultimately determine their weekend. With Larson’s lead only five points over Bell, every position matters. A victory could completely change the championship picture, while a crash could leave a contender with an enormous deficit. Sunday’s race promises to deliver another unpredictable Talladega showdown as NASCAR’s championship battle approaches its conclusion.

item.description: Amorim: ‘There was no game’ as 10-man Milan punished in Bournemouth Ruben Amorim insists ‘there was no game’ for Milan against Bournemouth, as the going down to 10 men after 28 minutes made it impossible to avoid a 3-0 defeat . ‘We cannot do that.’ The coach famously had a dismal record against Bournemouth on the Manchester United bench, including a 3-0 defeat here, and he continued that trend at the Vitality Stadium. They paid the price for two early naïve errors, the Koni De Winter handball for the opening Justin Kluivert penalty, then Mike Maignan’s shove on Tyler Adams prompting the double whammy of a red card and new penalty, converted by Marcus Tavernier. Amine Adli added a third late on with a free kick, and goal difference could be decisive in this Europa League format. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) “The penalty on the corner and the red card changed everything, so it was not a game. It was not a game,” Amorim told Sky Sport Italia. “We didn’t have time to recover from the first penalty. item.title: Rangers Given Clear Warning Over Celtic Title Race: Can McInnes Exploit Their European Advantage?
item.description: Rangers Given Clear Warning Over Celtic Title Race: Can McInnes Exploit Their European Advantage? Rangers have little room for another domestic slip-up if they want to close the gap on Celtic in the Scottish Premiership. With no European fixtures to manage, Derek McInnes’ side have a clear advantage in their pursuit of the league leaders, but recent results suggest they still need greater consistency. The Ibrox side missed a valuable opportunity last weekend. Rangers surrendered a lead to draw 2-2 against Dundee on October 17, allowing Celtic to strengthen their position with a crushing 7-1 victory over Hearts the following day. That result left the Light Blues four points behind their city rivals, increasing the pressure ahead of Saturday’s home match against St Johnstone. According to comments reported in the Scottish football discussion on The Breakdown podcast, relayed by BBC , former Rangers midfielder Kevin Thomson believes the fixture schedule should favour McInnes’ team over the coming weeks. Rangers have no continental matches after their European qualifying campaign ended in defeat on penalties against Jablonec. Celtic, meanwhile, have at least six more Europa League fixtures to negotiate, beginning with Thursday’s home meeting with Celta Vigo. Thomson argued that playing before Celtic allows Rangers to put their rivals under pressure. A victory against St Johnstone could cut the deficit to one point before Martin O’Neill’s side visit Hibernian on Sunday. The former midfielder also suggested that Rangers could supply more players than Celtic in a combined Old Firm starting XI, reflecting his confidence in the squad’s individual quality. “The bit I think that favours Rangers, or it should, and there can’t be any excuses from a blue perspective, is they’ve not got Europe,” former Rangers midfielder Thomson said on The Breakdown podcast. “The likelihood is they’re going to play in front of Celtic week after week. The Germans took the lead shortly before the break as Tim Lemperle's throw-in was loose inside the box until the ball found Kramaric, who headed it into the goal. Adam Daghim then doubled their advantage in the 49th. Kramaric received the ball near the penalty area and passed it to the left, where Noham Kamara accidentally set up Daghim, who cleverly slotted the ball into the lower-left corner. Hoffenheim were finally able to celebrate the three points once Adam Hložek sealed the win in the 83rd. The German side intercepted a sloppy pass from Lyon and the ball again ended up with Kramaric, who served Hložek's effort. The victory comes as huge relief for Hoffenheim. Before Thursday's game, they had only won three out of nine games in all competitions - none of them in the Europa League.

Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
